jsonataExerciser.followEditors.description: Keep the Exerciser linked to what you show in its panes: a JSON file you open (e.g. from the Explorer) is moved into the left editor group and becomes the input; a .jsonata file is moved into the top-right group and becomes the expression.

jsonataExerciser.autoEvaluate.description: Re-evaluate the expression automatically while typing (real-time output).

jsonataExerciser.debounceMs.description: Delay in milliseconds between the last keystroke and the evaluation.

jsonataExerciser.evaluationTimeoutMs.description: Evaluations running longer than this are aborted (protects against endless recursion).

jsonataExerciser.format.printWidth.description: Maximum line width used by the JSONata formatter.

enumDescriptions: Keep an object multi-line if you put a line break after its opening brace; otherwise collapse it if it fits (like Prettier for JavaScript).
Always put every key of an object constructor on its own line.
Plugin default: collapse objects that fit into the line width.
jsonataExerciser.format.objectLayout.description: Line break handling for JSONata object constructors { ... } when formatting.

jsonataExerciser.intellisense.fieldSugge.description: Suggest field names found in the Exerciser input JSON.

jsonataExerciser.ai.registerMcpServerInV.description: Also register the bundled MCP server with VS Code. Not needed for GitHub Copilot (it uses the built-in language model tools); useful if you want the same tools via the MCP list. Requires reload.

jsonataExerciser.inspect.live.description: Show the value of the sub-expression under the cursor (or the selection) as an inline hint while you move through the expression in the Exerciser. Toggle with 'JSONata: Toggle Live Value Inspection'.

jsonataExerciser.inspect.maxLength.description: Maximum length of the inline value hint.

languageModelTools.name: jsonata_evaluate
languageModelTools.userDescription: Evaluate a JSONata expression against JSON input locally.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Evaluates a JSONata expression against JSON data locally with the official jsonata library and returns the pretty-printed result or the JSONata error (code, message, position). ALWAYS use this to test an expression before presenting it. Pass the data inline (`input`) or, for files in the workspace, by path (`inputFile`, workspace-relative or absolute); the expression inline (`expression`) or by path (`expressionFile`).

expressionFile.description: Path of a .jsonata file to use instead of `expression` (workspace-relative or absolute).

input.description: The input JSON document as a JSON string.

inputFile.description: Path of a JSON file to use as input instead of `input` (workspace-relative or absolute). Preferred for large files.

languageModelTools.name: jsonata_inspect
languageModelTools.displayName: Inspect part of a JSONata expression
languageModelTools.userDescription: Evaluate one sub-expression in its real context (step-through debugging).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Step-through debugging for JSONata: evaluates ONE sub-expression of a larger expression, in its real context, and returns the value(s) it produced (once per evaluation, e.g. per array item) plus a step-by-step breakdown for dotted paths like a.b.c. Use it to find out where an expression returns nothing or a wrong value, instead of guessing. `part` must be exact text taken from the expression. Pass data inline (`input`) or by path (`inputFile`).

expressionFile.description: Path of a .jsonata file instead of `expression`.

part.description: Exact text of the sub-expression to inspect, e.g. "orders.items.price" or "price * qty".

occurrence.description: Which occurrence of `part` in the expression (0 = first).

inputFile.description: Path of a JSON file as input.

languageModelTools.name: jsonata_validate
languageModelTools.userDescription: Check the syntax of a JSONata expression.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Parses a JSONata expression with the official jsonata parser and reports syntax errors and unknown $function calls with their positions. Does not evaluate.

languageModelTools.name: jsonata_inputStructure
languageModelTools.userDescription: Outline of a JSON document (keys, nesting, arrays) to help write JSONata paths.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a compact outline of a JSON document: key names, value types, nesting, array boundaries, optional keys, sample values and example JSONata leaf paths. Use it before writing a JSONata expression so paths use the exact key names. Without arguments it describes the JSONata Exerciser input; or pass `input` (JSON text) or `inputFile` (path).

languageModelTools.name: jsonata_guide
languageModelTools.userDescription: JSONata cheat sheet, function list and recommended workflow.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a JSONata 2.x cheat sheet (paths, predicates, grouping, operators, common mistakes), the full list of built-in function signatures and the recommended workflow for writing expressions. Call it if you are unsure about JSONata syntax; JSONata is NOT JavaScript.

languageModelTools.name: jsonata_getExerciser
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read the expression, input and current result from the JSONata Exerciser.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns everything about the user's open JSONata Exerciser: input and expression file names, the current expression, its result or error, a compact outline of the input JSON structure (key names, nesting, arrays) and the beginning of the input data. Call this FIRST whenever the user mentions their JSON, 'the data', 'my expression', 'the error' or 'the output', or asks you to write or fix a JSONata expression.

languageModelTools.name: jsonata_updateExerciser
languageModelTools.userDescription: Replace the expression and/or input in the JSONata Exerciser.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Replaces the expression and/or the input JSON shown in the user's JSONata Exerciser and returns the new result. Only use after the user asked you to change or apply something; it overwrites what they have typed.
